subject: ventures/pwa-installability-check
professional: a front-end / PWA engineer who ships installable web apps and gates manifests in CI (the person who debugs 'Add to Home Screen not showing' against Chrome's install criteria)

evidence.correctness: Ran `node check.mjs` against a local server (127.0.0.1:8765) with three fixtures. (1) Manifest {name, display:standalone, one 192x192 png icon}, no start_url, no 512 icon: tool exits 0 and prints 'clears the checks ... the same criteria Lighthouse's installable-manifest audit checks'. Independent source: web.dev 'Installation criteria' / Chrome install criteria (as I recall them; web access was not used, so this is recall, not a fetched quote) require name or short_name, start_url, display in standalone/fullscreen/minimal-ui, icons including 192 AND 512, HTTPS, and prefer_related_applications not true. Missing start_url and missing 512 icon are install blockers there, but this tool downgrades both to 'notice' and exits 0. (2) Icon with purpose 'monochrome' only, sizes '192x192 512x512': counted as satisfying both size checks (purpose is collected in probe.mjs but never read in analyze.mjs); Chrome/MDN treat monochrome-only icons as not usable for the install icon (recall, hedged). (3) display 'browser' / absent -> danger, matches spec default and criteria: correct. (4) http://127.0.0.1 and localhost -> secure, matches secure-context rule; [::1] and *.localhost are not recognised as secure in probe.mjs (the [::1] run failed to connect so this was read from code, not exercised). (5) A 404 page with no manifest link is reported as 'No <link rel=manifest>' with no mention of the HTTP 404 (probe.mjs fetchText sets ok:true for any HTTP status). display_override and prefer_related_applications are ignored. Display, name, icon-size parsing and unreachable-icon logic were right; the install-criteria set is incomplete, so a developer can be told 'installable' when Chrome will not offer install. Not a 3 because of a confident wrong 'ok' on a common case.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README feature: manifest present/reachable (works), name (works), display mode (works), secure origin (works), 192 icon fetched and confirmed image (works), 3 notices (work as described), CLI exit codes 0/1/2 (worked: 0 on installable, 1 on no-manifest, 2 handled in code), --json output (code read; shape {target, probe} consumed by index.html paste flow), browser page renders pasted JSON (page.test.mjs structure only; not loaded in a browser). Companion pages vs-lighthouse.html and vs-reading-the-manifest-by-eye.html and add-to-home-screen-not-showing.html exist. Everything the README lists exists and works; no stubs or TODOs found. The gap is in what the README chose to list (see correctness), not in unfinished items.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/pwa-installability-check && node --test *.test.mjs`: 73 pass, 0 fail, ~0.4 s. Seeded mutation 1: analyze.mjs iconMeetsMinSize `s >= minPx` -> `s > minPx`: 3 tests failed (compliant manifest, 512 notice, runCheck), reverted with git checkout. Seeded mutation 2: added 'browser' to REQUIRED_DISPLAY_MODES: 1 test failed ('display: browser explicitly is a danger'), reverted. Working tree clean afterwards. Weaknesses: tests encode the author's reading of the criteria (a fully compliant manifest fixture has start_url and 512 icon, so nothing tests that the criteria themselves match Chrome); no golden test against a real Chrome/Lighthouse result; probe.mjs uses an injected fake fetch only, no local-server test; page tests check structure, not behaviour in a browser.
evidence.craft: Read analyze.mjs, probe.mjs, check.mjs, parts of index.html. Pure classification core separated from I/O with an injectable probe: good. Defects: probe USER_AGENT points at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address, not marisstella.app (probe.mjs:13); HTML link discovery is a regex over the whole document, so a commented-out or in-script `<link rel=manifest>` is matched (probe.mjs findManifestHref); page HTTP status is never checked, so 404/500 HTML is analysed as a page; icon fetch drains unbounded bodies with no size cap; `purpose` is collected then ignored; the 192-or-512 check duplicates the 'reachable' test per icon and `evidence` strings repeat; check.mjs main() guard `import.meta.url === file://${process.argv[1]}` breaks on paths with spaces or on Windows; --timeout with a non-numeric value yields NaN and silently falls back to the default (`timeoutMs ? ...`). Acceptable but not senior-clean.
evidence.claims: README, analyze.mjs header and index.html FAQ say the tool runs 'the same checks Lighthouse's installable-manifest audit runs' and that 'a report from this tool and a Lighthouse report should never disagree'. Run (1) above shows they do disagree: start_url and 512 icon are failures in Chrome's published criteria, notices here. Backed claims: no network except the target (probe.mjs read: true), usage counter stores no URLs (usage.mjs read, usage.test.mjs), disclaimer and no-warranty text present (README, page.test.mjs). Also: vs-lighthouse and the FAQ say Lighthouse checks an 'offline-capable service worker' for installability; Chrome dropped the service worker requirement (desktop 2022, Android later) and Lighthouse's PWA category was removed in v12, so that comparison is dated (recalled, not fetched). VENTURE.yaml stage 'prototype' with all hypotheses untested is honest. The headline equivalence claim is unbacked and contradicted by a run.
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a dev whose Add-to-Home-Screen prompt does not show runs the CLI on their staging URL. For the commonest real causes (missing 512 icon, missing start_url, wrong icon purpose) the tool exits 0 and says it clears the Lighthouse criteria, so the user would conclude the manifest is fine and keep debugging elsewhere. As a CI gate it will pass manifests Chrome rejects. It does correctly catch missing manifest, bad display, no name, no HTTPS and dead icon URLs, and the plain-English output and exit codes are usable. Browser page cannot fetch (explained honestly), requiring a paste step.
evidence.domain: Compared against Chrome's installability criteria (web.dev installation criteria; MDN 'Making PWAs installable'). Matches: name/short_name, display modes, HTTPS/localhost, 192 icon, spec default of 'browser'. Departs: start_url and 512x512 icon treated as notices (criteria list them as required); icon purpose ignored; display_override and prefer_related_applications not evaluated; manifest not resolved the way browsers do (e.g. 'sizes' with non-square entries uses min side, fine). A PWA engineer would say this is a decent first-pass lint, not the install-criteria check it claims to be. Sources were recalled, not fetched, which is why correctness and domain are not higher even where the tool agrees.

defects.what: Manifest with no start_url and no 512x512 icon exits 0 and prints 'clears the same criteria as Lighthouse installable-manifest'; Chrome's published install criteria require both. Both are downgraded to notices.
Headline claim that this tool and Lighthouse 'should never disagree' is false per the run above; repeated in README, analyze.mjs header and index.html FAQ.
Icon `purpose` is collected but never evaluated: a monochrome-only icon satisfies the 192 and 512 checks.
Page HTTP status is not checked: a 404/500 HTML body is analysed and reported as 'No <link rel=manifest>' with no mention of the status.
defects.where: ventures/pwa-installability-check/probe.mjs:fetchText (ok:true for any status) and analyze.mjs buildReport page check

defects.what: Comparison pages claim Lighthouse checks an offline service worker as part of installability; this is out of date (service worker no longer required by Chrome; Lighthouse 12 removed the PWA category).
USER_AGENT cites the retired GitHub Pages address.
Manifest link found by regex over raw HTML, so commented-out or in-script link tags match.
[::1] and *.localhost not treated as secure; non-numeric --timeout silently becomes the default; import.meta.url main guard fragile on paths with spaces.
No test compares classification against any external reference (Chrome/Lighthouse output); fixtures encode the author's reading of the criteria.

verdict: A tidy, well-tested, honestly scoped prototype whose core claim is wrong in a way users would act on. The code runs, 73 tests pass and two seeded mutations were caught, and the checks it does implement (name, display, HTTPS, reachable 192 icon, dead icons) behave correctly in a live run against a local server. But it declares a manifest installable, exit 0 and 'same criteria as Lighthouse', when start_url and a 512x512 icon are missing, both of which Chrome's published criteria require, and it ignores icon purpose. Because the benchmark sources were recalled rather than fetched, the correctness score is capped and the finding should be re-confirmed against web.dev before the fix. Does not meet the bar (claims 1, correctness 2); finished in the sense that everything it lists works (completeness 3).
